name: Chest press
cue: Keep your shoulder blades pinned and drive your elbows toward each other.
research: research.json biomech.chest_press: seated against a pad reclined ~12 deg, hips 80, knees 90, feet flat; shoulder elevation 70 -> 80 in a plane -20 -> 75 deg, elbow 105 -> 10. Handle path horizontal at mid-chest, 45-55 cm long, converging so the hands finish about shoulder width in front of the lower chest. Machine: converging swing levers on near-vertical pivots outboard of and in front of the knees (tools/design/chest_press_v2.mjs, CP_T=0.23 CP_HUB=0.44): each post rises to just below handle height and carries a short, level lever arm beside the hand, so the levers never cross the chest, the face or the lap from the camera (a hub at knee height made the near lever a long diagonal across the lap). IK pole "fk": the elbows follow the authored arm keys, so they stay in line with the handle through the press. Handles: start (0.265, 0.515, 0.100) with elbows ~25 deg behind the frontal plane, lockout (0.118, 0.522, 0.319): hands 0.24 H apart, elbow ~12 deg, plane ~78 deg. Elevation at lockout reads ~67: the research 80 assumes shoulder-height handles; the researched mid-chest handles with the 12 deg recline put the arm ~10 deg below that. Load: a selectorized weight stack behind the back post (two guide rods, cap pulley, cable into the frame) rises 0.1 H over the press. (tools/design/loads.mjs)

camera.note: Research view is az 75 (profile turned 15 deg toward the front, as research best_camera suggests). Turned another 15 deg toward the chest and raised 16 deg: the horizontal adduction happens in the transverse plane, and looking down on it lets the pecs read above the converging arms at lockout. The machine stands on a floor rail (stack, back post, seat post), a cross rail between the lever posts and a foot plate under the feet, not a plate under everything: from this camera the plate ran below the arc under the exercise name.

targets.note: shoulder_elevation tol 15: research end 80 assumes shoulder-height handles (see research); with the researched mid-chest handles the straight arm at lockout reads 69.6. The elbow path uses the FK pole, so the elevation runs 62.6 -> 69.6 with no mid-press sag (a fixed pole [1, -0.6, -0.5] dropped it to 57 mid-rep).
